articles.title: The biggest biotech funding rounds in October 2026
articles.text:
Skip to content Suggested Topics: Home In Depth The biggest biotech funding rounds in October 2026 Photo credits: Andre Taissin (Unsplash) Add Labiotech as your Google Preferred Source Newsletter Signup - Under Article / In Page " * " indicates required fields The companies Summit Therapeutics, Dren Bio, and Lycia Therapeutics bagged the biggest biotech funding rounds overall in October 2026 across private and public funding types. In this article, we break down last month’s private and public fundraising activity, looking at the largest rounds in more detail. Table of contents Private biotech funding rounds in October 2026 First, let’s take a look at the private biotech investments in October 2026, breaking them down by value, location, funding type, and therapeutic subsector. Biggest private biotech funding rounds by value October 2026 saw Summit Therapeutics secure the biggest biotech funding round of the month by some distance, after AstraZeneca completed a $2 billion strategic investment in the company. The equity investment will allow for the accelerated development of ivonescimab, a PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, across a number of solid tumor settings, including combinations with antibody drug conjugates (ADCs). The drug candidate is currently being tested in multiple phase 3 trials. Dren Bio came second in the standings last month after closing a $350 million private financing, which will support continued late-stage clinical development, regulatory submission, and planned commercial launch of dibotatug (DR-01), Dren Bio’s pathogenic cell-depleting antibody that is in late-stage development for the treatment of rare blood cancers and other hematologic and autoimmune diseases. Meanwhile, in third place, U.K.-based biotech OMass Therapeutics raised $310 million (£230 million) in a series C round to support the advancement of the company’s lead program, OMS1620, a potential best-in-class melanocortin-2 (MC2) receptor antagonist, through phase 2 of clinical development in congenital adrenal hyperplasia, as well as ACTH-dependent Cushing’s syndrome. Private biotech funding rounds by location North American companies came out on top again last month in terms of number of rounds and amount raised, bringing in $3.439 billion from 10 rounds; this huge total can largely be credited to Summit’s $2 billion equity investment from AstraZeneca. European companies, meanwhile, also performed quite well in October, attracting $667 million from eight rounds. However, it was a bad month for the Asia-Pacific region, with no significant rounds taking place. Private biotech funding rounds by funding type When we look at the private biotech funding statistics in November by funding type, we can see that there were more series A and series B rounds than any other, with four each; however, series B rounds came out on top here in terms of the total amount raised, bringing in $391 million compared to the $268 million brought in by series A rounds. Nevertheless, the category of strategic equity investments brought in the largest total overall, thanks again to AstraZeneca’s $2 billion commitment to Summit. It’s also worth noting that a couple of companies raised their totals through combined rounds – for example, Estuary Biotherapeutics secured a total of $103 million through a $93 million series A round and a $10 million seed round. Suggested Articles The biggest biotech funding rounds in September 2026 The biggest biotech funding rounds in August 2026 The biggest biotech funding rounds in July 2026 The biggest biotech funding rounds in June 2026 The biggest biotech funding rounds in May 2026 Private biotech funding rounds by therapeutic subsector Although the therapeutic subsectors of artificial intelligence (AI) and oncology both came out on top in terms of the number of rounds last month, with four each, oncology companies brought home the largest amount of money, attracting $2.565 billion compared to AI’s $335 million. Public biotech funding rounds in October 2026 Now, let’s check out the public biotech fundraising rounds that occurred in October 2026, breaking them down by value and therapeutic subsector. Public biotech funding by value Lycia Therapeutics ranked first in the public fundraising standings in November 2026 after attracting $317.5 million from its initial public offering (IPO). The company is focused on the discovery and development of novel therapies designed to degrade disease-causing extracellular proteins. The funding will help it to advance its lead candidates: LCA-0061, a cataLYTAC degrader of IgE for food allergy and other allergic diseases, and LCA-0321, a LYTAC degrader designed to selectively deplete the autoantibodies that cause Graves’ disease. Meanwhile, in joint second place last month, City Therapeutics and Recursion both raised $200 million; City’s funding came from an IPO and will help it with its goal of engineering the next generation of RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics, while Recursion’s funding came from an underwritten offering and will help it to continue its work on AI-enabled drug discovery . In third place, Bambusa Therapeutics bagged $168.9 million from its IPO. The company is developing long-acting precision bispecific antibodies designed to redefine standards of care in immunology and inflammation. Its pipeline includes BBT001, a bispecific antibody targeting IL-4Rα and IL-31 in clinical development for atopic dermatitis and other inflammatory skin diseases; BBT002, a bispecific antibody targeting IL-4Rα and IL-5 in clinical development for type 2 inflammatory disorders; and preclinical programs BBT003 and BBT004 focused on gastroenterology and autoantibody-driven autoimmune diseases, respectively. Public biotech funding by therapeutic subsector The immunological disease therapeutic subsector came out on top last month in the public biotech fundraising standings, attracting a total of $603.1 million from three rounds. Meanwhile, AI followed in second place, bringing in $350 million from two rounds. Month-to-month comparison of biotech fundraising Below is a graph showing a month-to-month comparison of private and public biotech fundraising, looking at the total amount of money raised per month in 2026. October 2026 was an excellent month for private biotech fundraising, with companies raising $4.106 billion. This is the second-highest total of the year for private companies, coming in just behind May’s total of $4.266 billion. Meanwhile, for public companies, October was a relatively average month in terms of the total raised, as companies brought home $1.339 billion. Nevertheless, this is an improvement on September’s total, and it was a good month for IPOs, which made up seven of the eight public fundraising rounds last month. Public biotech funding by value Lycia Therapeutics ranked first in the public fundraising standings in November 2026 after attracting $317.5 million from its initial public offering (IPO). The company is focused on the discovery and development of novel therapies designed to degrade disease-causing extracellular proteins. The funding will help it to advance its lead candidates: LCA-0061, a cataLYTAC degrader of IgE for food allergy and other allergic diseases, and LCA-0321, a LYTAC degrader designed to selectively deplete the autoantibodies that cause Graves’ disease. Meanwhile, in joint second place last month, City Therapeutics and Recursion both raised $200 million; City’s funding came from an IPO and will help it with its goal of engineering the next generation of RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics, while Recursion’s funding came from an underwritten offering and will help it to continue its work on AI-enabled drug discovery . In third place, Bambusa Therapeutics bagged $168.9 million from its IPO. The company is developing long-acting precision bispecific antibodies designed to redefine standards of care in immunology and inflammation. Its pipeline includes BBT001, a bispecific antibody targeting IL-4Rα and IL-31 in clinical development for atopic dermatitis and other inflammatory skin diseases; BBT002, a bispecific antibody targeting IL-4Rα and IL-5 in clinical development for type 2 inflammatory disorders; and preclinical programs BBT003 and BBT004 focused on gastroenterology and autoantibody-driven autoimmune diseases, respectively.
